final_method_items.summary: Expand string move (memcpy) ot store (memset) operation. Use i386 string operations when profitable. The code depends upon architecture, block size and alignment, but always has one of the following overall structures: Aligned move sequence: 1) Prologue guard: Conditional that jumps up to epilogues for small blocks that can be handled by epilogue alone. This is faster but also needed for correctness, since prologue assume the block is larger than the desired alignment. Optional dynamic check for size and libcall for large blocks is emitted here too, with -minline-stringops-dynamically. 2) Prologue: copy first few bytes in order to get destination aligned to DESIRED_ALIGN. It is emitted only when ALIGN is less than DESIRED_ALIGN and up to DESIRED_ALIGN - ALIGN bytes can be copied. We emit either a jump tree on power of two sized blocks, or a byte loop. 3) Main body: the copying loop itself, copying in SIZE_NEEDED chunks with specified algorithm. 4) Epilogue: code copying tail of the block that is too small to be handled by main body (or up to size guarded by prologue guard). Misaligned move sequence 1) missaligned move prologue/epilogue containing: a) Prologue handling small memory

behavior_items: The reproducer uses C23 `_BitInt` support with a non-power-of-two precision, specifically a 465-bit integer type. That forces GCC to represent the value as a large aggregate-like object rather than a normal scalar register value on x86-64, so code generation must use block moves, block clears, or libcall-style expansion instead of a single machine instruction.

The critical statement is `b = a >> 1860;`, where the shift count is far larger than the bit width of the left operand. Since 1860 is greater than 465, the source is exercising GCC's handling of an extreme overshift on an extended-width integer type.

For C shift semantics, a right shift by a count greater than or equal to the promoted width is undefined behavior. Even so, GCC must still survive compilation and either optimize the expression away, fold it to some internal form, or emit code conservatively. The bug is therefore not a wrong-code issue in defined semantics, but an internal compiler robustness failure triggered while lowering this UB case.

Because the destination `b` is a large `_BitInt(465)` object, GCC appears to lower the result production into storage operations that include clearing bytes for the destination object. The stack trace shows the failure path through `expand_builtin_memset_args`, `clear_storage_hints`, and `set_storage_via_setmem`, which means the compiler decided to materialize some or all of the result by zero-filling memory rather than by scalar instruction synthesis.

The failure happens in the RTL `expand` pass, not during parsing or front-end folding. This indicates the front end and gimplification accepted the `_BitInt` expression, but the back end later tried to expand a memory-set sequence for the large object and hit an invalid assumption.

The x86-specific ICE occurs in `expand_set_or_cpymem_prologue_epilogue_by_misaligned_moves` inside `config/i386/i386-expand.cc`. That routine is part of GCC's logic for implementing `memset`/`memcpy`-style operations using vector or chunked moves when alignment is imperfect, so the testcase specifically exercises x86 block-operation expansion rather than generic tree-level shift folding alone.

The command-line options are essential to reaching the crash path. `-O2` encourages simplification and builtin expansion; `-mavx512f` enables wide vector move strategies; and `-mstore-max=128` biases the backend toward using large inlined store sequences up to 128 bytes. Together they make GCC choose the x86 inline setmem implementation that enters the crashing helper.

The chosen store strategy is especially relevant because a 465-bit object occupies 59 bytes, which is awkwardly misaligned and not naturally sized to a common vector width. That means prologue/epilogue handling for partial chunks or misaligned heads/tails becomes necessary, exactly the area named in the ICE site.

The reproducer therefore combines three stressors: a very wide unusual integer precision, an obviously out-of-range shift count, and target options that force aggressive inline memory clearing with AVX-512-capable block moves. The interaction exposes a backend assumption bug in how the x86 expander handles the generated setmem operation for this case.

The backtrace showing `gen_setmemsi` and `ix86_expand_set_or_cpymem` suggests GCC did not simply constant-fold the overshift to a scalar zero in a trivial way. Instead, it likely formed a large zero result object and then delegated initialization of that object to the block-store expander, where the internal consistency check or unsupported case triggered the ICE.

Since the report labels this as a regression on GCC 16, the exercised behavior is likely tied to recent changes either in `_BitInt` lowering, x86 setmem expansion heuristics, or the interaction between `-mstore-max` and AVX-512-based misaligned move generation. Older compilers presumably either folded the case differently or used a safer expansion path.

In short, the reproducer is not testing runtime correctness of the shift itself; it is testing whether GCC can safely compile a pathological `_BitInt` overshift under x86 optimization settings. The observed compiler behavior is an internal compiler error during backend expansion of a memory-clear sequence derived from that expression.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: This reproducer drives GCC into an ICE by assigning the result of an extreme right shift on a 465-bit `_BitInt` to another 465-bit object under `-O2 -mavx512f -mstore-max=128`. The overshift is undefined in C, but GCC should still compile it without crashing. Instead, GCC lowers the large `_BitInt` result through a zero-initialization or setmem path, then the x86 backend chooses an AVX-512/misaligned inline store expansion and aborts in `expand_set_or_cpymem_prologue_epilogue_by_misaligned_moves`. The testcase therefore exercises the interaction between wide `_BitInt` lowering, UB overshift handling, and x86 block-store expansion heuristics, exposing a regression in GCC 16's RTL expand stage.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The common pattern is that the source expression is not crashing in front-end `_BitInt` parsing or tree folding, but only after GCC lowers a large `_BitInt(465)` result into a memory object and tries to materialize an all-zero result through the generic clear/setmem path. The triggering shape is consistent: a non-register-sized `_BitInt` object (59 bytes), an overshift (`a >> 1860`) that likely canonicalizes to a zero-valued object, and x86 options (`-mavx512f -mstore-max=128`) that force inline block-store expansion with wide misaligned moves. The backtrace shows the exact transition from shift/result lowering into `expand_builtin_memset_args` -> `clear_storage_hints` -> `set_storage_via_setmem` -> `gen_setmemsi` -> `ix86_expand_set_or_cpymem` -> `expand_set_or_cpymem_prologue_epilogue_by_misaligned_moves`, so the bug pattern is not shift semantics itself but a backend robustness failure when expanding a memset-like operation for an oddly sized `_BitInt` aggregate. Because 59 bytes is neither a natural scalar width nor a clean AVX-512 chunk size, the x86 expander must generate head/tail or prologue/epilogue stores, and the ICE strongly suggests a violated invariant there: likely an assumption that the remaining size, piece mode, vector width, or misalignment state always matches a supported store pattern. Since the report says regression in GCC 16, the most plausible defect area is recent x86 block-operation expansion changes or changed `_BitInt` lowering that now routes this UB overshift through an inline AVX-512 setmem path that earlier compilers avoided or handled safely.
possible_causes: A defect in `config/i386/i386-expand.cc` where `expand_set_or_cpymem_prologue_epilogue_by_misaligned_moves` assumes the tail/prologue size for inline setmem is representable by a supported move mode, but `_BitInt(465)` zero-initialization creates a 59-byte clear that leaves an unsupported remainder and triggers an internal consistency abort.

A bug in x86 `setmem` expansion heuristics causing `ix86_expand_set_or_cpymem` to select the AVX-512 misaligned-move strategy for a constant-size clear that should have fallen back to a safer byte/word store sequence or library call, especially under `-mstore-max=128`.

Incorrect interaction between generic `_BitInt` lowering and block-clear expansion: the overshift result is converted into a bulk zeroing operation without preserving size/alignment constraints expected by the i386 backend, so the backend receives a malformed or unsupported `setmem` request.

A regression in handling constant-size clears whose object size is not a multiple of vector width, where prologue/epilogue generation on x86 mishandles the final partial chunk when AVX-512 is enabled and `-mstore-max` encourages large inline stores.

A target-specific bug where the emitted `gen_setmemsi` operands or associated alignment/expected-size metadata are inconsistent for large nonstandard integer objects, leading `expand_set_or_cpymem_prologue_epilogue_by_misaligned_moves` to see an impossible mode, count, or offset combination.

A missing robustness fallback for undefined-behavior overshift results on large `_BitInt` types: even if middle-end simplifies the value to zero, the backend path chosen for storing that zero object does not defend against unusual aggregate widths introduced by `_BitInt` and crashes instead of degrading to scalarized stores or libcall expansion.
evidence: The ICE site is x86-specific: `expand_set_or_cpymem_prologue_epilogue_by_misaligned_moves` in `config/i386/i386-expand.cc`, directly pointing at block set/copy expansion rather than `_BitInt` parsing.

The backtrace goes through `expand_builtin_memset_args`, `clear_storage_hints`, and `set_storage_via_setmem`, showing GCC is clearing storage for the result object rather than emitting a normal scalar shift instruction.
`_BitInt(465)` occupies 59 bytes on x86-64, an awkward non-power-of-two object size that naturally stresses misaligned prologue/epilogue logic in inline memset expansion.
The crash requires `-O2 -mavx512f -mstore-max=128`, which are precisely the kinds of options that steer x86 toward aggressive inline vectorized setmem lowering instead of conservative fallback code.

The expression `a >> 1860` is an extreme overshift relative to width 465, so middle-end likely recognizes a zero-like result and hands the backend a bulk-clear operation; the failure occurs after that lowering choice, not during semantic diagnosis.
The report is marked as a GCC 16 regression, which matches a likely recent defect in either `_BitInt` lowering to storage ops or x86 AVX-512 setmem strategy selection/invariant checking.

The set of allowed stack pointer modifications is small: (1) One or more auto-inc style memory references (aka pushes), (2) One or more addition/subtraction with the SP as destination, (3) A single move insn with the SP as destination, (4) A call_pop insn, (5) Noreturn call insns if !ACCUMULATE_OUTGOING_ARGS. Insns in the sequence that do not modify the SP are ignored, except for noreturn calls. The return value is the amount of adjustment that can be trivially verified, via immediate operand or auto-inc. EXTRA is the amount in bytes of extra space to leave next to this arg. This is ignored if an argument block has already been allocated. On a machine that lacks real push insns, ARGS_ADDR is the address of the bottom of the argument block for this call. We use indexing off there to store the arg. On mac

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static void store_constructor_field (rtx target, poly_uint64 bitsize, poly_int64 bitpos, poly_uint64 bitregion_start, poly_uint64 bitregion_end, machine_mode mode, tree exp, int cleared, alias_set_type alias_set, bool reverse)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Helper function for store_constructor. TARGET, BITSIZE, BITPOS, MODE, EXP are as for store_field. CLEARED is as for store_constructor. ALIAS_SET is the alias set to use for any stores. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order. This provides a recursive shortcut back to store_constructor when it isn't necessary to go through store_field. This is so that we can pass through the cleared field to let store_constructor know that we may not have to clear a substructure if the outer structure has already been cleared.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static int fields_length (const_tree type)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Returns the number of FIELD_DECLs in TYPE.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void store_constructor (tree exp, rtx target, int cleared, poly_int64 size, bool reverse)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Store the value of constructor EXP into the rtx TARGET. TARGET is either a REG or a MEM; we know it cannot conflict, since safe_from_p has been called. CLEARED is true if TARGET is known to have been zero'd. SIZE is the number of bytes of TARGET we are allowed to modify: this may not be the same as the size of EXP if we are assigning to a field which has been packed to exclude padding bits. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static rtx store_field (rtx target, poly_int64 bitsize, poly_int64 bitpos, poly_uint64 bitregion_start, poly_uint64 bitregion_end, machine_mode mode, tree exp, alias_set_type alias_set, bool nontemporal, bool reverse)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Store the value of EXP (an expression tree) into a subfield of TARGET which has mode MODE and occupies BITSIZE bits, starting BITPOS bits from the start of TARGET. If MODE is VOIDmode, it means that we are storing into a bit-field. BITREGION_START is bitpos of the first bitfield in this region. BITREGION_END is the bitpos of the ending bitfield in this region. These two fields are 0, if the C++ memory model does not apply, or we are not interested in keeping track of bitfield regions. Always return const0_rtx unless we have something particular to return. ALIAS_SET is the alias set for the destination. This value will (in general) be different from that for TARGET, since TARGET is a reference to the containing structure. If NONTEMPORAL is true, try generating a nontemporal store. If REVERSE is true, the store is to be done in reverse order.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: tree get_inner_reference (tree exp, poly_int64 *pbitsize, poly_int64 *pbitpos, tree *poffset, machine_mode *pmode, int *punsignedp, int *preversep, int *pvolatilep)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Given an expression EXP that may be a COMPONENT_REF, a BIT_FIELD_REF, an ARRAY_REF, or an ARRAY_RANGE_REF, look for nested operations of these codes and find the ultimate containing object, which we return. We set *PBITSIZE to the size in bits that we want, *PBITPOS to the bit position, *PUNSIGNEDP to the signedness and *PREVERSEP to the storage order of the field. If the position of the field is variable, we store a tree giving the variable offset (in units) in *POFFSET. This offset is in addition to the bit position. If the position is not variable, we store 0 in *POFFSET. If any of the extraction expressions is volatile, we store 1 in *PVOLATILEP. Otherwise we don't change that. If the field is a non-BLKmode bit-field, *PMODE is set to VOIDmode. Otherwise, it is a mode that can be used to access the field. If the field describes a variable-sized object, *PMODE is set to BLKmode and *PBITSIZE is set to -1. An access cannot be made in this case, but the address of the object can be found.

gcc/expr.cc.summary: expand_expr: generate code for computing expression EXP. An rtx for the computed value is returned. The value is never null. In the case of a void EXP, const0_rtx is returned. The value may be stored in TARGET if TARGET is nonzero. TARGET is just a suggestion; callers must assume that the rtx returned may not be the same as TARGET. If TARGET is CONST0_RTX, it means that the value will be ignored. If TMODE is not VOIDmode, it suggests generating the result in mode TMODE. But this is done only when convenient. Otherwise, TMODE is ignored and the value generated in its natural mode. TMODE is just a suggestion; callers must assume that the rtx returned may not have mode TMODE. Note that TARGET may have neither TMODE nor MODE. In that case, it probably will not be used. If MODIFIER is EXPAND_SUM then when EXP is an addition we can return an rtx of the form (MULT (REG ...) (CONST_INT ...)) or a nest of (PLUS ...) and (MINUS ...) where the terms are products as above, or REG or MEM, or constant. Ordinarily in such cases we would output mul or add instructions and then return a pseudo reg containing the sum. EXPAND_INITIALIZER is much like EXPAND_SUM except that it also marks a label as ab

gcc/expr.cc.signature: tree string_constant (tree arg, tree *ptr_offset, tree *mem_size, tree *decl)

If we return nonzero, set *PTR_OFFSET to the (possibly non-constant) offset in bytes within the string that ARG is accessing. If MEM_SIZE is non-zero the storage size of the memory is returned. gcc/expr.cc.signature: enum tree_code maybe_optimize_pow2p_mod_cmp (enum tree_code code, tree *arg0, tree *arg1)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Optimize x % C1 == C2 for signed modulo if C1 is a power of two and C2 is non-zero and C3 ((1<<(prec-1)) | (C1 - 1)): for C2 > 0 to x & C3 == C2 for C2 < 0 to x & C3 == (C2 & C3).

gcc/expr.cc.signature: enum tree_code maybe_optimize_mod_cmp (enum tree_code code, tree *arg0, tree *arg1)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Attempt to optimize unsigned (X % C1) == C2 (or (X % C1) != C2). If C1 is odd to: (X - C2) * C3 <= C4 (or >), where C3 is modular multiplicative inverse of C1 and 1<<prec and C4 is ((1<<prec) - 1) / C1 or ((1<<prec) - 1) / C1 - 1 (the latter if C2 > ((1<<prec) - 1) % C1). If C1 is even, S = ctz (C1) and C2 is 0, use ((X * C3) r>> S) <= C4, where C3 is modular multiplicative inverse of C1>>S and 1<<prec and C4 is (((1<<prec) - 1) / (C1>>S)) >> S. For signed (X % C1) == 0 if C1 is odd to (all operations in it unsigned): (X * C3) + C4 <= 2 * C4, where C3 is modular multiplicative inverse of (unsigned) C1 and 1<<prec and C4 is ((1<<(prec - 1) - 1) / C1). If C1 is even, S = ctz(C1), use ((X * C3) + C4) r>> S <= (C4 >> (S - 1)) where C3 is modular multiplicative inverse of (unsigned)(C1>>S) and 1<<prec and C4 is ((1<<(prec - 1) - 1) / (C1>>S)) & (-1<<S). See the Hacker's Delight book, section 10-17.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void maybe_optimize_sub_cmp_0 (enum tree_code code, tree *arg0, tree *arg1)

gcc/expr.cc.summary: Expand CODE with arguments INNER & (1<<BITNUM) and 0 that represents a single bit equality/inequality test, returns where the result is located.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static rtx do_store_flag (const_sepops ops, rtx target, machine_mode mode)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Generate code to calculate OPS, and exploded expression using a store-flag instruction and return an rtx for the result. OPS reflects a comparison. If TARGET is nonzero, store the result there if convenient. Return zero if there is no suitable set-flag instruction available on this machine. Once expand_expr has been called on the arguments of the comparison, we are committed to doing the store flag, since it is not safe to re-evaluate the expression. We emit the store-flag insn by calling emit_store_flag, but only expand the arguments if we have a reason to believe that emit_store_flag will be successful. If we think that it will, but it isn't, we have to simulate the store-flag with a set/jump/set sequence.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: bool try_casesi (tree index_type, tree index_expr, tree minval, tree range, rtx table_label, rtx default_label, rtx fallback_label, profile_probability default_probability)

MODE is its expected mode (needed if INDEX is constant). RANGE is the length of the jump table. TABLE_LABEL is a CODE_LABEL rtx for the table itself. DEFAULT_LABEL is a CODE_LABEL rtx to jump to if the index value is out of range. DEFAULT_PROBABILITY is the probability of jumping to the default label.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static rtx assemble_crc_table (unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT polynom, unsigned short crc_bits)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Assemble CRC table with 256 elements for the given POLYNOM and CRC_BITS. POLYNOM is the polynomial used to calculate the CRC table's elements. CRC_BITS is the size of CRC, may be 8, 16, ... .

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static rtx generate_crc_table (unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT polynom, unsigned short crc_bits)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Generate CRC lookup table by calculating CRC for all possible 8-bit data values. The table is stored with a specific name in the read-only static data section. POLYNOM is the polynomial used to calculate the CRC table's elements. CRC_BITS is the size of CRC, may be 8, 16, ... .

gcc/expr.cc.signature: static void calculate_table_based_CRC (rtx *crc, const rtx &input_data, const rtx &polynomial, machine_mode data_mode)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Generate table-based CRC code for the given CRC, INPUT_DATA and the POLYNOMIAL (without leading 1). First, using POLYNOMIAL's value generates CRC table of 256 elements, then generates the assembly for the following code, where crc_bit_size and data_bit_size may be 8, 16, 32, 64, depending on CRC: for (int i = 0; i < data_bit_size / 8; i++) crc = (crc << 8) ^ crc_table[(crc >> (crc_bit_size - 8)) ^ (data >> (data_bit_size - (i + 1) * 8) & 0xFF))]; So to take values from the table, we need 8-bit data. If input data size is not 8, then first we extract upper 8 bits, then the other 8 bits, and so on.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void expand_crc_table_based (rtx op0, rtx op1, rtx op2, rtx op3, machine_mode data_mode)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Generate table-based CRC code for the given CRC, INPUT_DATA and the POLYNOMIAL (without leading 1). CRC is OP1, data is OP2 and the polynomial is OP3. This must generate a CRC table and an assembly for the following code, where crc_bit_size and data_bit_size may be 8, 16, 32, 64: uint_crc_bit_size_t crc_crc_bit_size (uint_crc_bit_size_t crc_init, uint_data_bit_size_t data, size_t size) { uint_crc_bit_size_t crc = crc_init; for (int i = 0; i < data_bit_size / 8; i++) crc = (crc << 8) ^ crc_table[(crc >> (crc_bit_size - 8)) ^ (data >> (data_bit_size - (i + 1) * 8) & 0xFF))]; return crc; }

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void gen_common_operation_to_reflect (rtx *op, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT and1_value, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT and2_value, unsigned shift_val)

gcc/expr.cc.summary: Reflect 16-bit value for the 16-bit target.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void generate_reflecting_code_standard (rtx *op)
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Generate instruction sequence which reflects the value of the OP using shift, and, or operations. OP's mode may be less than word_mode.

gcc/expr.cc.signature: void expand_reversed_crc_table_based (rtx op0, rtx op1, rtx op2, rtx op3, machine_mode data_mode, void (*gen_reflecting_code) (rtx *op))
gcc/expr.cc.summary: Generate table-based reversed CRC code for the given CRC, INPUT_DATA and the POLYNOMIAL (without leading 1). CRC is OP1, data is OP2 and the polynomial is OP3. This must generate CRC table and assembly for the following code, where crc_bit_size and data_bit_size may be 8, 16, 32, 64: uint_crc_bit_size_t crc_crc_bit_size (uint_crc_bit_size_t crc_init, uint_data_bit_size_t data, size_t size) { reflect (crc_init) uint_crc_bit_size_t crc = crc_init; reflect (data); for (int i = 0; i < data_bit_size / 8; i++) crc = (crc << 8) ^ crc_table[(crc >> (crc_bit_size - 8)) ^ (data >> (data_bit_size - (i + 1) * 8) & 0xFF))]; reflect (crc); return crc; }

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static bool is_builtin_name (const char *name)

gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return true if NODE should be considered for inline expansion regardless of the optimization level. This means whenever a function is invoked with its "internal" name, which normally contains the prefix "__builtin".

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool get_object_alignment_2 (tree exp, unsigned int *alignp, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT *bitposp, bool addr_p)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Compute values M and N such that M divides (address of EXP - N) and such that N < M. If these numbers can be determined, store M in alignp and N in BITPOSP and return true. Otherwise return false and store BITS_PER_UNIT to alignp and any bit-offset to *bitposp. Note that the address (and thus the alignment) computed here is based on the address to which a symbol resolves, whereas DECL_ALIGN is based on the address at which an object is actually located. These two addresses are not always the same. For example, on ARM targets, the address &foo of a Thumb function foo() has the lowest bit set, whereas foo() itself starts on an even address. If ADDR_P is true we are taking the address of the memory reference EXP and thus cannot rely on the access taking place.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool get_object_alignment_1 (tree exp, unsigned int *alignp, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT *bitposp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: For a memory reference expression EXP compute values M and N such that M divides (&EXP - N) and such that N < M. If these numbers can be determined, store M in alignp and N in *BITPOSP and return true. Otherwise return false and store BITS_PER_UNIT to *alignp and any bit-offset to *bitposp.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: unsigned int get_object_alignment (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return the alignment in bits of EXP, an object.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool get_pointer_alignment_1 (tree exp, unsigned int *alignp, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT *bitposp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: For a pointer valued expression EXP compute values M and N such that M divides (EXP - N) and such that N < M. If these numbers can be determined, store M in alignp and N in *BITPOSP and return true. Return false if the results are just a conservative approximation. If EXP is not a pointer, false is returned too.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: unsigned int get_pointer_alignment (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return the alignment in bits of EXP, a pointer valued expression. The alignment returned is, by default, the alignment of the thing that EXP points to. If it is not a POINTER_TYPE, 0 is returned. Otherwise, look at the expression to see if we can do better, i.e., if the expression is actually pointing at an object whose alignment is tighter.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: unsigned string_length (const void *ptr, unsigned eltsize, unsigned maxelts)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return the number of leading non-zero elements in the sequence [ PTR, PTR + MAXELTS ) where each element's size is ELTSIZE bytes. ELTSIZE must be a power of 2 less than 8. Used by c_strlen.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: tree c_strlen (tree arg, int only_value, c_strlen_data *data, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Compute the length of a null-terminated character string or wide character string handling character sizes of 1, 2, and 4 bytes. TREE_STRING_LENGTH is not the right way because it evaluates to the size of the character array in bytes (as opposed to characters) and because it can contain a zero byte in the middle. ONLY_VALUE should be nonzero if the result is not going to be emitted into the instruction stream and zero if it is going to be expanded. E.g. with i++ ? "foo" : "bar", if ONLY_VALUE is nonzero, constant 3 is returned, otherwise NULL, since len = c_strlen (ARG, 1); if (len) expand_expr (len, ...); would not evaluate the side-effects. If ONLY_VALUE is two then we do not emit warnings about out-of-bound accesses. Note that this implies the result is not going to be emitted into the instruction stream. Additional information about the string accessed may be recorded in DATA. For example, if ARG references an unterminated string, then the declaration will be stored in the DECL field. If the length of the unterminated string can be determined, it'll be stored in the LEN field. Note this length could well be different than what a C strlen call would return. ELTSIZE is 1 for norm

The strategy is to issue one store_by_pieces for each power of two, from most to least significant, guarded by a test on whether there are at least that many bytes left to copy in LEN. ??? Should we skip some powers of two in favor of loops? Maybe start at the max of TO/LEN/word alignment, at least when optimizing for size, instead of ensuring O(log len) dynamic compares?

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_bswap (machine_mode target_mode, tree exp, rtx target, rtx subtarget)

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_unop (machine_mode target_mode, tree exp, rtx target, rtx subtarget, optab op_optab)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to a unary builtin in EXP. Return NULL_RTX if a normal call should be emitted rather than expanding the function in-line. If convenient, the result should be placed in TARGET. SUBTARGET may be used as the target for computing one of EXP's operands.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_expect (tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to __builtin_expect. We just return our argument as the builtin_expect semantic should've been already executed by tree branch prediction pass.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_expect_with_probability (tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to __builtin_expect_with_probability. We just return our argument as the builtin_expect semantic should've been already executed by tree branch prediction pass.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_assume_aligned (tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to __builtin_assume_aligned. We just return our first argument as the builtin_assume_aligned semantic should've been already executed by CCP.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: void expand_builtin_trap (void)
static void expand_builtin_unreachable (void)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to __builtin_unreachable. We do nothing except emit a barrier saying that control flow will not pass here. It is the responsibility of the program being compiled to ensure that control flow does never reach __builtin_unreachable.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_fabs (tree exp, rtx target, rtx subtarget)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand EXP, a call to fabs, fabsf or fabsl. Return NULL_RTX if a normal call should be emitted rather than expanding the function inline. If convenient, the result should be placed in TARGET. SUBTARGET may be used as the target for computing the operand.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_copysign (tree exp, rtx target, rtx subtarget)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand EXP, a call to copysign, copysignf, or copysignl. Return NULL is a normal call should be emitted rather than expanding the function inline. If convenient, the result should be placed in TARGET. SUBTARGET may be used as the target for computing the operand.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: void default_emit_call_builtin___clear_cache (rtx begin, rtx end)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Emit a call to __builtin___clear_cache.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: void maybe_emit_call_builtin___clear_cache (rtx begin, rtx end)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Emit a call to __builtin___clear_cache, unless the target specifies it as do-nothing. This function can be used by trampoline finalizers to duplicate the effects of expanding a call to the clear_cache builtin.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static void expand_builtin___clear_cache (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to __builtin___clear_cache.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx round_trampoline_addr (rtx tramp)

static rtx expand_builtin_init_descriptor (tree exp)

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_adjust_descriptor (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to the builtin descriptor adjustment routine.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_signbit (tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the call EXP to the built-in signbit, signbitf or signbitl function. The function first checks whether the back end provides an insn to implement signbit for the respective mode. If not, it checks whether the floating point format of the value is such that the sign bit can be extracted. If that is not the case, error out. EXP is the expression that is a call to the builtin function; if convenient, the result should be placed in TARGET.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_fork_or_exec (tree fn, tree exp, rtx target, int ignore)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand fork or exec calls. TARGET is the desired target of the call. EXP is the call. FN is the identificator of the actual function. IGNORE is nonzero if the value is to be ignored.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static inline machine_mode get_builtin_sync_mode (int fcode_diff)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Reconstitute a mode for a __sync intrinsic operation. Since the type of the pointer in these functions is void*, the tree optimizers may remove casts. The mode computed in expand_builtin isn't reliable either, due to __sync_bool_compare_and_swap. FCODE_DIFF should be fcode - base, where base is the FOO_1 code for the group of builtins. This gives us log2 of the mode size.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx get_builtin_sync_mem (tree loc, machine_mode mode)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the memory expression LOC and return the appropriate memory operand for the builtin_sync operations.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_expr_force_mode (tree exp, machine_mode mode)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Make sure an argument is in the right mode. EXP is the tree argument. MODE is the mode it should be in.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_sync_operation (machine_mode mode, tree exp, enum rtx_code code, bool after, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __sync_xxx_and_fetch and __sync_fetch_and_xxx intrinsics. EXP is the CALL_EXPR. CODE is the rtx code that corresponds to the arithmetic or logical operation from the name; an exception here is that NOT actually means NAND. TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results; AFTER is true if this is the fetch_and_xxx form.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_compare_and_swap (machine_mode mode, tree exp, bool is_bool, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __sync_val_compare_and_swap and __sync_bool_compare_and_swap intrinsics. EXP is the CALL_EXPR. IS_BOOL is true if this is the boolean form. TARGET is a place for us to store the results; this is NOT optional if IS_BOOL is true.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_sync_lock_test_and_set (machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __sync_lock_test_and_set intrinsic. Note that the most general form is actually an atomic exchange, and some targets only support a reduced form with the second argument being a constant 1. EXP is the CALL_EXPR; TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_sync_lock_release (machine_mode mode, tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __sync_lock_release intrinsic. EXP is the CALL_EXPR.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static enum memmodel get_memmodel (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Given an integer representing an ``enum memmodel'', verify its correctness and return the memory model enum.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_exchange (machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_exchange intrinsic: TYPE __atomic_exchange (TYPE *object, TYPE desired, enum memmodel) EXP is the CALL_EXPR. TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_compare_exchange (machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_compare_exchange intrinsic: bool __atomic_compare_exchange (TYPE *object, TYPE *expect, TYPE desired, BOOL weak, enum memmodel success, enum memmodel failure) EXP is the CALL_EXPR. TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static void expand_ifn_atomic_compare_exchange_into_call (gcall *call, machine_mode mode)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Helper function for expand_ifn_atomic_compare_exchange - expand internal ATOMIC_COMPARE_EXCHANGE call into __atomic_compare_exchange_N call. The weak parameter must be dropped to match the expected parameter list and the expected argument changed from value to pointer to memory slot.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: void expand_ifn_atomic_compare_exchange (gcall *call)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand IFN_ATOMIC_COMPARE_EXCHANGE internal function.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_load (machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_load intrinsic: TYPE __atomic_load (TYPE *object, enum memmodel) EXP is the CALL_EXPR. TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_store (machine_mode mode, tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_store intrinsic: void __atomic_store (TYPE *object, TYPE desired, enum memmodel) EXP is the CALL_EXPR. TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_fetch_op (machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target, enum rtx_code code, bool fetch_after, bool ignore, enum built_in_function ext_call)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_fetch_XXX intrinsic: TYPE __atomic_fetch_XXX (TYPE *object, TYPE val, enum memmodel) EXP is the CALL_EXPR. TARGET is an optional place for us to store the results. CODE is the operation, PLUS, MINUS, ADD, XOR, or IOR. FETCH_AFTER is true if returning the result of the operation. FETCH_AFTER is false if returning the value before the operation. IGNORE is true if the result is not used. EXT_CALL is the correct builtin for an external call if this cannot be resolved to an instruction sequence.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: void expand_ifn_atomic_bit_test_and (gcall *call)

gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand IFN_ATOMIC_*_FETCH_CMP_0 internal function.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_clear (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand an atomic clear operation. void _atomic_clear (BOOL *obj, enum memmodel) EXP is the call expression.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_test_and_set (tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand an atomic test_and_set operation. bool _atomic_test_and_set (BOOL *obj, enum memmodel) EXP is the call expression.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_atomic_always_lock_free (tree arg0, tree arg1)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return true if (optional) argument ARG1 of size ARG0 is always lock free on this architecture. If ARG1 is NULL, use typical alignment for size ARG0.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_always_lock_free (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return true if the parameters to call EXP represent an object which will always generate lock free instructions. The first argument represents the size of the object, and the second parameter is a pointer to the object itself. If NULL is passed for the object, then the result is based on typical alignment for an object of the specified size. Otherwise return false.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_atomic_is_lock_free (tree arg0, tree arg1)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return a one or zero if it can be determined that object ARG1 of size ARG is lock free on this architecture.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_atomic_is_lock_free (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return true if the parameters to call EXP represent an object which will always generate lock free instructions. The first argument represents the size of the object, and the second parameter is a pointer to the object itself. If NULL is passed for the object, then the result is based on typical alignment for an object of the specified size. Otherwise return NULL

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static void expand_builtin_atomic_thread_fence (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_thread_fence intrinsic: void __atomic_thread_fence (enum memmodel) EXP is the CALL_EXPR.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static void expand_builtin_atomic_signal_fence (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __atomic_signal_fence intrinsic: void __atomic_signal_fence (enum memmodel) EXP is the CALL_EXPR.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static void expand_builtin_sync_synchronize (void)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand the __sync_synchronize intrinsic.

static void expand_builtin_set_thread_pointer (tree exp)

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_stack_save (void)

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_builtin_goacc_parlevel_id_size (tree exp, rtx target, int ignore)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Emit code to get the openacc gang, worker or vector id or size.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx inline_string_cmp (rtx target, tree var_str, const char *const_str, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT length, int const_str_n, machine_mode mode)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a string compare operation using a sequence of char comparison to get rid of the calling overhead, with result going to TARGET if that's convenient. VAR_STR is the variable string source; CONST_STR is the constant string source; LENGTH is the number of chars to compare; CONST_STR_N indicates which source string is the constant string; IS_MEMCMP indicates whether it's a memcmp or strcmp. to: (assume const_str_n is 2, i.e., arg2 is a constant string) target = (int) (unsigned char) var_str[0] - (int) (unsigned char) const_str[0]; if (target != 0) goto ne_label; ... target = (int) (unsigned char) var_str[length - 2] - (int) (unsigned char) const_str[length - 2]; if (target != 0) goto ne_label; target = (int) (unsigned char) var_str[length - 1] - (int) (unsigned char) const_str[length - 1]; ne_label:

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx inline_expand_builtin_bytecmp (tree exp, rtx target)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Inline expansion of a call to str(n)cmp and memcmp, with result going to TARGET if that's convenient. If the call is not been inlined, return NULL_RTX.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static rtx expand_speculation_safe_value (machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target, bool ignore)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand a call to __builtin_speculation_safe_value_<N>. MODE represents the size of the first argument to that call, or VOIDmode if the argument is a pointer. IGNORE will be true if the result isn't used.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: rtx expand_builtin_crc_table_based (internal_fn fn, scalar_mode crc_mode, scalar_mode data_mode, machine_mode mode, tree exp, rtx target)

gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Expand an expression EXP that calls a built-in function, with result going to TARGET if that's convenient (and in mode MODE if that's convenient). SUBTARGET may be used as the target for computing one of EXP's operands. IGNORE is nonzero if the value is to be ignored.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: enum built_in_function builtin_mathfn_code (const_tree t)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Determine whether a tree node represents a call to a built-in function. If the tree T is a call to a built-in function with the right number of arguments of the appropriate types, return the DECL_FUNCTION_CODE of the call, e.g. BUILT_IN_SQRT. Otherwise the return value is END_BUILTINS.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_constant_p (tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to __builtin_constant_p, if we know its argument ARG will evaluate to a constant.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree build_builtin_expect_predicate (location_t loc, tree pred, tree expected, tree predictor, tree probability)

Fortran FE can also produce builtin_expect with PREDICTOR as third argument. builtin_expect_with_probability instead uses third argument as PROBABILITY value.

gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to builtin_expect with arguments ARG0, ARG1, ARG2, ARG3. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification is possible.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_classify_type (tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to __builtin_classify_type with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_strlen (location_t loc, tree expr, tree type, tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call EXPR (which may be null) to __builtin_strlen with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_inf (location_t loc, tree type, int warn)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to __builtin_inf or __builtin_huge_val.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_sincos (location_t loc, tree arg0, tree arg1, tree arg2)

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_memcmp (location_t loc, tree arg1, tree arg2, tree len)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin memcmp with arguments ARG1 and ARG2. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification can be made.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_isascii (location_t loc, tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to builtin isascii with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_toascii (location_t loc, tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to builtin toascii with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_isdigit (location_t loc, tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to builtin isdigit with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_fabs (location_t loc, tree arg, tree type)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to fabs, fabsf or fabsl with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_abs (location_t loc, tree arg, tree type)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to abs, labs, llabs, imaxabs, uabs, ulabs, ullabs or uimaxabs with argument ARG.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_carg (location_t loc, tree arg, tree type)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to builtin carg(a+bi) -> atan2(b,a).

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_frexp (location_t loc, tree arg0, tree arg1, tree rettype)

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_modf (location_t loc, tree arg0, tree arg1, tree rettype)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to builtin modf.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_interclass_mathfn (location_t loc, tree fndecl, tree arg)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Given a location LOC, an interclass builtin function decl FNDECL and its single argument ARG, return an folded expression computing the same, or NULL_TREE if we either couldn't or didn't want to fold (the latter happen if there's an RTL instruction available).

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_classify (location_t loc, tree fndecl, tree arg, int builtin_index)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to __builtin_isnan(), __builtin_isinf, __builtin_finite. ARG is the argument for the call.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_fpclassify (location_t loc, tree *args, int nargs)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to __builtin_fpclassify(int, int, int, int, int, ...). This builtin will generate code to return the appropriate floating point classification depending on the value of the floating point number passed in. The possible return values must be supplied as int arguments to the call in the following order: FP_NAN, FP_INFINITE, FP_NORMAL, FP_SUBNORMAL and FP_ZERO. The ellipses is for exactly one floating point argument which is "type generic".

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_unordered_cmp (location_t loc, tree fndecl, tree arg0, tree arg1, enum tree_code unordered_code, enum tree_code ordered_code)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Fold a call to an unordered comparison function such as __builtin_isgreater(). UNORDERED_CODE and ORDERED_CODE are comparison codes that give the opposite of the desired result. UNORDERED_CODE is used for modes that can hold NaNs and ORDERED_CODE is used for the rest.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static tree fold_builtin_iseqsig (location_t loc, tree arg0, tree arg1)

Examples: VEC_UNPACK_HI/LO_EXPR, VEC_WIDEN_MULT_HI/LO_EXPR In this case OP0 and optionally OP1 would be initialized, but WIDE_OP wouldn't (not relevant for this case). 2) Operations whose result is of the same size as the last argument to the operation, but wider than all the other arguments to the operation. Since we are only interested in the lower 2 words, partial result (3) and the upper words of (2a) and (2b) don't need to be calculated. Hence (2a) and (2b) can be calculated using non-widening multiplication. (1), however, needs to be calculated with an unsigned widening multiplication. If this operation is

gcc/optabs.cc.signature: static rtx expand_doubleword_mod (machine_mode mode, rtx op0, rtx op1, bool unsignedp)
gcc/optabs.cc.summary: Subroutine of expand_binop. Optimize unsigned double-word OP0 % OP1 for constant OP1. If for some bit in [BITS_PER_WORD / 2, BITS_PER_WORD] range (prefer higher bits) ((1w << bit) % OP1) == 1, then the modulo can be computed in word-mode as ((OP0 & (bit - 1)) + ((OP0 >> bit) & (bit - 1)) + (OP0 >> (2 * bit))) % OP1. Whether we need to sum 2, 3 or 4 values depends on the bit value, if 2, then carry from the addition needs to be added too, i.e. like: sum += __builtin_add_overflow (low, high, &sum) Optimize signed double-word OP0 % OP1 similarly, just apply some correction factor to the sum before doing unsigned remainder, in the form of sum += (((signed) OP0 >> (2 * BITS_PER_WORD - 1)) & const); then perform unsigned remainder = sum % OP1; and finally remainder += ((signed) OP0 >> (2 * BITS_PER_WORD - 1)) & (1 - OP1);

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool can_refer_decl_in_current_unit_p (tree decl, tree from_decl)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true when DECL can be referenced from current unit. FROM_DECL (if non-null) specify constructor of variable DECL was taken from. We can get declarations that are not possible to reference for various reasons: 1) When analyzing C++ virtual tables. C++ virtual tables do have known constructors even when they are keyed to other compilation unit. Those tables can contain pointers to methods and vars in other units. Those methods have both STATIC and EXTERNAL set. 2) In WHOPR mode devirtualization might lead to reference to method that was partitioned elsehwere. In this case we have static VAR_DECL or FUNCTION_DECL that has no corresponding callgraph/varpool node declaring the body. 3) COMDAT functions referred by external vtables that we devirtualize only during final compilation stage. At this time we already decided that we will not output the function body and thus we can't reference the symbol directly.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true if EXPR is an acceptable right-hand-side for a GIMPLE assignment. We validate the entire tree, not just the root node, thus catching expressions that embed complex operands that are not permitted in GIMPLE. This function is needed because the folding routines in fold-const.cc may return such expressions in some cases, e.g., an array access with an embedded index addition. It may make more sense to have folding routines that are sensitive to the constraints on GIMPLE operands, rather than abandoning any any attempt to fold if the usual folding turns out to be too aggressive.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Convert EXPR into a GIMPLE value suitable for substitution on the RHS of an assignment. Insert the necessary statements before iterator *SI_P. The statement at *SI_P, which must be a GIMPLE_CALL is replaced. If the call is expected to produces a result, then it is replaced by an assignment of the new RHS to the result variable. If the result is to be ignored, then the call is replaced by a GIMPLE_NOP. A proper VDEF chain is retained by making the first VUSE and the last VDEF of the whole sequence be the same as the replaced statement and using new SSA names for stores in between.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool get_range_strlen (tree arg, bitmap visited, strlen_range_kind rkind, c_strlen_data *pdata, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: For an ARG referencing one or more strings, try to obtain the range of their lengths, or the size of the largest array ARG referes to if the range of lengths cannot be determined, and store all in *PDATA. For an integer ARG (when RKIND == SRK_INT_VALUE), try to determine the maximum constant value. If ARG is an SSA_NAME, follow its use-def chains. When RKIND == SRK_STRLEN, then if PDATA->MAXLEN is not equal to the determined length or if we are unable to determine the length, return false. VISITED is a bitmap of visited variables. RKIND determines the kind of value or range to obtain (see strlen_range_kind). Set PDATA->DECL if ARG refers to an unterminated constant array. On input, set ELTSIZE to 1 for normal single byte character strings, and either 2 or 4 for wide characer strings (the size of wchar_t). Return true if *PDATA was successfully populated and false otherwise.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: bool get_range_strlen (tree arg, c_strlen_data *pdata, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Try to obtain the range of the lengths of the string(s) referenced by ARG, or the size of the largest array ARG refers to if the range of lengths cannot be determined, and store all in *PDATA which must be zero-initialized on input except PDATA->MAXBOUND may be set to a non-null tree node other than INTEGER_CST to request to have it set to the length of the longest string in a PHI. ELTSIZE is the expected size of the string element in bytes: 1 for char and some power of 2 for wide characters. Return true if the range [PDATA->MINLEN, PDATA->MAXLEN] is suitable for optimization. Returning false means that a nonzero PDATA->MINLEN doesn't reflect the true lower bound of the range when PDATA->MAXLEN is -1 (in that case, the actual range is indeterminate, i.e., [0, PTRDIFF_MAX - 2].

If an unterminated array is discovered and our caller handles unterminated arrays, then bubble up the offending DECL and return the maximum size. Otherwise return NULL.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strcat (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dst, tree src)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Simplify a call to the strcat builtin. DST and SRC are the arguments to the call. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification was possible, otherwise return the simplified form of the call as a tree. The simplified form may be a constant or other expression which computes the same value, but in a more efficient manner (including calls to other builtin functions). The call may contain arguments which need to be evaluated, but which are not useful to determine the result of the call. In this case we return a chain of COMPOUND_EXPRs. The LHS of each COMPOUND_EXPR will be an argument which must be evaluated. COMPOUND_EXPRs are chained through their RHS. The RHS of the last COMPOUND_EXPR in the chain will contain the tree for the simplified form of the builtin function call.

If NEGATE_P is true, we are negating all of IN, again except a literal for which we use *MINUS_LITP instead. If a variable part is of pointer type, it is negated after converting to TYPE. This prevents us from generating illegal MINUS pointer expression. LOC is the location of the converted variable part. If IN is itself a literal or constant, return it as appropriate. Hence leaving OEP_ONLY_CONST unset means assuming isochronic (or instantaneous) tree equivalence.
